# 02 Blend

Full definition: [TAXONOMY.md](../../TAXONOMY.md), section 3.

**What belongs here.** A and B mix by opacity. Nothing moves and no edge travels across the frame.

**Test.** Is every pixel a weighted mix of A and B (or a flat colour), with no moving boundary?

**Not here.** A dip to white with bloom is 09 Light › Flash. A dissolve through a designed texture map is 03 Wipe.

**Build.** Remotion built-in: fade().

## Subfamilies

| Folder | What goes in it | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| [Crossfade](crossfade/) | A fades out while B fades in. | standard dissolve, slow dream dissolve |
| [Dip to Colour](dip-to-colour/) | A fades to a flat colour, then B fades in from it. | dip to black, white, brand colour |
| [Luma Dissolve](luma-dissolve/) | The image's own brightness decides which pixels change first. | highlights-first dissolve |
| [Blend Mode](blend-mode/) | The mix uses a blend mode instead of normal opacity. | additive film dissolve, difference |

## Transitions in this family

| Transition | Subfamily | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [Crossfade](crossfade/crossfade/) | Crossfade | Scene A fades out while scene B fades in. The classic dissolve. |
| [Dip to Colour](dip-to-colour/dip-to-colour/) | Dip to Colour | Fades to a flat colour, holds, then fades up on the next scene. |
| [Luma Dissolve](luma-dissolve/luma-dissolve/) | Luma Dissolve | Scene A dissolves by its own brightness: its highlights vanish first and its shadows last, showing scene B behind. |
| [Film Dissolve](blend-mode/film-dissolve/) | Blend Mode | An additive dissolve: both scenes add together, so the midpoint glows like a film dissolve. |
